question_stem:
A sphere of radius $2.1\text{ mm}$ falls with terminal (constant) velocity through a liquid, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

Three forces act on the moving sphere. The weight of the sphere is $7.2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N}$ and the upthrust acting on it is $4.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N}$. The viscous force $F_V$ acting on the sphere is given by

$$F_V = krv$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere, $v$ is its velocity and $k$ is a constant. The value of $k$ in SI units is 17.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Determine the SI base units of $k$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the value of the upthrust acting on the sphere to calculate the density $\rho$ of the liquid.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: On the sphere in Fig. 1.1, draw three arrows to show the directions of the weight $W$, the upthrust $U$ and the viscous force $F_V$. Label these arrows $W$, $U$ and $F_V$ respectively.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the terminal (constant) velocity of the sphere.
